## Summary of the fix

The bug was caused by mutual clap `overrides_with` declarations between `--plain` and `--paging` in `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs`. When a user ran `bat --paging=never --plain`, clap's override semantics removed the `--paging` argument from the matches entirely, so bat fell back to auto-paging (and vice versa, `--paging=always --plain` dropped the plain style).

Changes:
1. `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs` — removed `.overrides_with("paging")` from the `plain` arg and `.overrides_with("plain")` from the `paging` arg, so the two options now compose independently instead of erasing each other.
2. `src/bin/bat/app.rs:160-183` — since overrides no longer provide last-wins ordering between the flags, added explicit ordering logic using `indices_of`: in `--paging=always` mode, a second `-p` (`-pp`) occurring after `--paging=always` still disables the pager, while `-pp --paging=always` enables it. This preserves the documented `-pp` behavior (matching how upstream bat resolved this issue).
